name: Carl Zeiss Jena MC Sonnar 180 mm f/ 2.8
merge_into: Carl Zeiss Jena Sonnar 180 mm f/ 2.8
note: Same 5-element/3-group Olympia-Sonnar recipe across the entire 50+ year run; MC is a coating generation = alias, per policy.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Biometar 80 mm f/ 2.8 T 1Q
merge_into: Carl Zeiss Jena Biometar 80 mm f/ 2.8
note: T is a coating mark and 1Q a DDR quality mark - variant engravings, never records. Same Zoellner 5-element Biometar; winner's mount pinned in corrections.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 80 mm f/ 2.8 (for Pentacon Six)
merge_into: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 80 mm f/ 2.8 T
note: One 4-element Tessar: developed for the Exakta 66, remounted for the Praktisix 1956-58, sold in Exakta and M42 for 35mm. The winner is then renamed to drop the T coating mark (NAME_FIXUPS, redirect preserved).

name: Prakticar 135 mm f/ 2.8 MC Pentacon
note: Scraped twin of the same Pentacon-made B-mount 135/2.8.

name: Prakticar 135 f2,8 MC
note: Decimal-comma scraped twin of the same lens.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena 135 mm f/ 2.8
note: The B-mount 2.8/135 was Pentacon-made (Meyer Orestor lineage) even when badged Carl Zeiss Jena P; folding the CZJ-badged row into the Prakticar record instead of renaming it - three twins already shipped and a rename would have minted a fourth.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Flektogon 20 mm f/ 4
note: Zebra Flektogon 4/20 amply attested in Exakta bayonet alongside M42; shipped row said M42 only.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Pancolar 50 mm f/ 1.8
note: Exakta-bayonet version made for the Exakta RTL 1000. Two optical versions (6/4 thoriated, later 6/5 MC) under one engraved name - one record. B-mount sibling is the curated Prakticar 50/1.8.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 40 mm f/ 4.5
note: Primarily an Exakta-mount lens (Kine Exakta through DDR-era T types); also produced in M42 and Praktina. Shipped row claimed M42 only.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Fernobjektiv 500 mm f/ 8
note: Postwar DDR version (1952) sold in Exakta, M42 and Praktina. Never a Pentacon Six lens. Fernobjektiv is the genuine CZJ catalog product name - keep it.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Biometar 120 mm f/ 2.8
note: Compact 35mm-format version announced Sept 1960 in Exakta, M42 and Praktina mounts; among the scarcest auto-diaphragm CZJ Exakta lenses. Same Zoellner 5-element design as the P6 lens.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Biometar 80 mm f/ 2.8
note: Post-fold pin after the T 1Q merge: 1950s compact version attested in M42 (red T) and Exakta. Same 5-element Zoellner design as the P6 standard lens.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Sonnar 300 mm f/ 4
note: Original 1951 T version sold in Exakta and M42; Praktisix/P6 version 1963, MC 1975. One optical lineage; shipped row claimed P6 only.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Sonnar 180 mm f/ 2.8
note: Post-fold pin after the MC merge. 1950s production sold in Exakta; P6 served as intermediate mount with CZJ adapters to 35mm mounts incl. M42. Same 5-element/3-group Olympia-Sonnar recipe throughout.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 50 mm f/ 2.8
note: Embargo export marking; contested names were shortened to initials (T=Tessar) per the Zeiss Namensstreit.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 50 mm f/ 3.5
note: Embargo alias, keyed on the post-rename name (the T coating mark left the canonical name via NAME_FIXUPS).

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Biotar 58 mm f/ 2
note: Embargo short code B=Biotar.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Biotar 75 mm f/ 1.5
note: Embargo short code B=Biotar.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Flektogon 35 mm f/ 2.8
note: F short code attested but rarer; zebra is the dominant seller spelling.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Flektogon 50 mm f/ 4
note: Seller spellings for the P6 wide-angle.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Flektogon 65 mm f/ 2.8
note: Seller spellings for the P6 wide-angle.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Sonnar 135 mm f/ 4
note: Keyed on the post-rename name. The real postwar SLR Sonnar 4/135 (1956/57-1969, Exakta/M42/Praktina); shipped mounts were CORRECT. Distinct from the prewar Contax RF Sonnar 4/135.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Sonnar 200 mm f/ 2.8
note: 1970s MC-era lens, M42 correct; the B-mount sibling is the shipped CZJ Prakticar 200/2.8 MC.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Jenazoom II 28-200 mm f/ 3.8-5.6
note: Keyed on the post-rename name. The Contax/Yashica mount claim traces to a single database with no independent confirmation. Badge-era zoom (Cosina/Sigma built, Jena name leased); null over guess.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Jenazoom II 70-210 mm f/ 2.8-4
note: Keyed on the post-rename name. Same as the 28-200: C/Y claim unverified, single-source.

name: Prakticar 135 mm f/ 2.8 MC
note: Post-fold pin for the four-way 135/2.8 consolidation: the B-mount Prakticar 2.8/135 was Pentacon-made (Meyer Orestor lineage); units badged Carl Zeiss Jena P were not made by CZJ. CZJ's own B-mount 135 was the f/3.5 (curated). Junk brand value 'Prakticar' replaced.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tele Tessar 180 mm f/ 6.3
note: Prewar Tele-Tessar K 6.3/18cm era lens; a Pentacon Six version cannot exist (P6 introduced 1956, no 180/6.3 in any P6 line list). Exakta kept as the attested half; P4 verifies the Contax RF/Flektoskop versions. Rename to hyphenated Tele-Tessar is spacing-only (id-stable).

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Prakticar 50 mm f/ 1.4 MC
note: Seller spellings. Two optically different versions (v1 1978-84 thoriated, v2 1982-90) under one engraved name - one record.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Macro-Prakticar 55 mm f/ 2.8
note: German catalog spelling Makro; CZJ-made new design.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Tessar 80 mm f/ 2.8
note: Post-fold, post-rename pin: one 4-element Tessar developed for the Exakta 66, remounted for the Praktisix, sold in Exakta and M42 for 35mm. Keyed on the final name after the (for Pentacon Six) fold and the T-mark rename.

name: Carl Zeiss Jena Jenazoom Super 75-300 mm f/ 4.5-5.6
note: The first-word-as-maker artifact left 75-300 as the manufacturer; the repair pass only reads the name when the value is junk-shaped, and a focal range is not in its junk class. Keyed on the post-rename name.
